## EMST role: Ecologist (state variant, lead level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:broadMatch`, confidence 0.4, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-wa:R20-ecologist/state:516N`). *Authority position (editorial):* advisor-researcher.

**Competency targets at this level (agent draft)**

- Assess and monitor biodiversity across species and habitats — lead L4 *(distinguishing)*
- Design monitoring and sampling for valid environmental inference — lead L4
- Assess species habitat requirements and habitat condition — lead L4
- Recognize and assess ecosystems that have crossed into novel states — lead L4
- Plan for ecological transformation with resist, accept or direct strategies — lead L4
- Analyze environmental data statistically and interpret the results — lead L4
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — lead L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — lead L1
- Read site history and reference conditions from landscape evidence — lead L3
- Identify organisms from field characters, specimens, images and recordings — lead L3
- Assess climate vulnerability of species, ecosystems, infrastructure and communities — lead L4
- Build, calibrate and validate predictive and simulation models of environmental systems — lead L3
- Assess ecosystem services with production-function models validated against observations — lead L3

**Main tasks at this level (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- Analyze long-term biodiversity monitoring data to estimate change in occupancy or richness against conservation objectives, stating uncertainty — 4.9% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Implement a multi-taxon biodiversity monitoring protocol at assigned sites, coordinating crews, passive detectors and sample collection to schedule — 4.8% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Report biodiversity monitoring findings to decision-makers with recommended protections, separating observed change from inference and stating its limits — 3.9% *(needed at entry)*
- Adjust the monitoring schedule or method mix at a site when disturbance, access loss or detector failure threatens the time series, recording the change — 3.9% *(needed at entry)*
- Measure habitat attributes such as cover, structure, water and forage at used and available sites following a habitat-use study protocol — 3.9% *(needed at entry)*
- Evaluate a habitat suitability map against field observations of use and condition, documenting where and why the model fails — 3.9%
- Evaluate whether a site's vegetation, soils and disturbance regime have moved beyond the historical range of variability, citing field and record evidence — 3.9%
- Assess ecological function and conservation value of a novel species assemblage at a site using field indicators of structure, process and habitat — 3.9% *(needed at entry)*
- Map potential climate refugia from topographic, hydrologic and climate data, stating the assumptions and validation of the refugia model. — 3.9% *(needed at entry)*
- Evaluate whether mapped refugia can support climate-sensitive species, using field and monitoring evidence of their current condition. — 3.9%
- Plan for imperfect detection in a monitoring design, choosing repeat visits or detection models suited to the methods used. — 3.9%
- Choose the mix of field, sensor, remote-sensing and community methods for a monitoring programme from cost, detection and comparability evidence. — 3.9% *(needed at entry)*
